title: Protocol for assessing the role of hippocampal perineuronal nets in aversive memories
protocol: Anesthetize mouse.
Weigh the animal.
Calculate the volume of 14 mg/mL working solution of avertin to be delivered.
Inject an appropriate volume of avertin intraperitoneally.
Return the animal to its home cage.
Determine that the mouse is fully anesthetized before proceeding.
Use indicators of deep pain recognition such as the pedal reflex, tail pinch reflex, and eyelid reflex.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to prevent eyes from drying.
Place the mouse in the stereotaxic instrument.
Hook the front teeth to the hole of the mouthpiece.
Fix the nose in place with the nose clamp.
Position ear bars against the skull, just behind the ears, to fix the head.
Shave the head using a small animal shaver or depilatory cream.
Disinfect the surgical area using 10% povidone/iodine solution and alcohol at least three times, ending with povidone/iodine.
Make an incision approximately 1 cm along the midline using surgical scissors or sterile scalpel.
Remove the periosteum using cotton swabs.
Dry the skull with fresh cotton swabs.
Adjust the head position so it is leveled.
Ensure bregma and lambda are at the same height.
Check that two points, equidistant from the sagittal suture, are at the same height.
Position the head so that bregma is in the center of the crossed lines of the centering scope using X- and Y-nobs.
Adjust the digital display of coordinates to show zero in both X- and Y-coordinates.
Remove the centering scope and fit the stereotaxic instrument with a drill.
Center the tip of the drill bit at bregma.
Move the drill along the X-axis to 1.8 mm posterior to bregma.
Move the drill laterally along the Y-axis to 1 mm.
Drill a hole.
If bleeding occurs, press a cotton swab to the hole until it stops.
Move the drill laterally along the Y-axis to 1 mm in the opposite direction.
Drill a hole.
Mix one scoop of dry carboxylate cement with one drop of liquid cement.
Adjust the mixture consistency by adding more dry or liquid cement as needed.
Insert an assembled cannula into the holes drilled in the skull.
Affix the cannula using the prepared carboxylate cement.
Hold the cannula in place with forceps while applying the cement around it.
Pull the skin and adhere it to the cement around the cannula to close the wound.
Apply 4% lidocaine gel (or another local anesthetic) to the skin to alleviate pain immediately after surgery.
Sterilize the instruments in the glass bead sterilizer.
Place the mouse on a heating pad at 37°C until it awakens (1–2 h).
House the mice individually before starting infusions and behavioral experiments.
Monitor the mice regularly until they awaken.
Allow at least one week of post-surgical recovery before proceeding with infusions and behavioral tests.
Assemble the equipment as shown in Figure 4A.
Fit Hamilton syringes with tubing.
Connect tubing to the infusion pump.
Remove dust cap and dummy cannula from the mouse head cannula.
Insert an injector into the cannula.
Prepare two 25 μL Hamilton syringes filled with water.
If air bubbles are present, forcefully empty the syringe into a 1.5 mL tube and refill until no bubbles remain.
Place prepared syringes into the infusion pump.
Fit injector with tubing connected to syringes.
Remove air from tubing and injector by pushing the syringe plunger until a small water drop appears on the tips of the injector.
Set the infusion volume to 250 nL.
Set the infusion rate to 150 nL/min.
Fill the infusion apparatus with ChABC solution.
Pull the syringe plungers out until a very small air bubble is formed.
Insert the injector into the tube containing ChABC solution and pull the plungers gently.
Monitor that air bubbles are moving up while the tubing fills with ChABC solution.
Move the pusher of the infusion pump until it presses against the syringe plungers.
Infuse ChABC into CA1.
Anesthetize a mouse in the induction chamber, setting the concentration of isoflurane to 5%.
Monitor breathing closely during anesthesia.
Remove mouse from induction chamber when anesthetized.
Transfer mouse to assembled infusion equipment.
Set concentration of isoflurane to 1.4%.
Hold base of guide cannula tightly with forceps.
Unscrew cap and pull out dummy cannula.
Insert injector into the cannula.
Mark position of air bubble in tubing with marker.
Start infusion through the injector.
Leave injector in place for 1 minute after infusion.
Remove injector slowly from guide cannula.
Insert dummy cannula back into guide cannula.
Screw cap onto guide cannula securely.
Return mouse to home cage.
Train mice in a behavioral paradigm using contextual fear conditioning.
Expose mice to a context for 3 min followed by a 2 s, 0.8 mA footshock.
Re-expose mice to the box for 3 min to test freezing behavior.
Monitor and record the session using a camera fitted within a constantly illuminated box.
Determine freezing response, horizontal activity, exploratory activity, and shock bursts during testing.
Record freezing by trained observers unaware of experimental conditions.
Analyze infrared beam signals from the context for other data.
Use different groups of mice for each experimental condition (vehicle/ChABC).
Test separate groups of mice for recent and remote memory to avoid reconsolidation or fear extinction effects.
Clean the fear conditioning chamber with 70% ethanol.
Transfer a mouse from the home cage into the fear conditioning chamber.
Start the program: 3 min context; 2 s, 0.8 mA footshock.
Record whether mouse is freezing every 10 seconds by briefly observing the mouse’s behavior.
Note whether the mouse responds to the electric shock.
Return the mouse to home cage.
Repeat the procedure for each mouse.
Pause point: The experiment is paused until the recent memory test day.
Perform recent memory test on day 4 after training.
Expose the mouse to the context for 3 minutes during the recent memory test.
Perform remote memory test on day 21 (or days 21-35).
Perfuse animals one day after the remote test with ice-cold 4% paraformaldehyde in phosphate buffer (pH 7.4) following a standard transcardial perfusion protocol.
Remove brains and post-fix for 24 hours in the same fixative.
Immerse brains in 20% sucrose in phosphate buffer for 24 hours.
Immerse brains in 30% sucrose in phosphate buffer for 24 hours.
Freeze brains in an embedding medium (such as Tissue-Plus O.C.T. Compound).
Cut 50 μm sections on a cryostat.
Store sections in 1× PBS/0.4 mg/mL thimerosal at 4°C.
Wash sections in 1 x phosphate buffered saline, pH 7.4 (PBS)/0.04 mg/mL thimerosal for 5 min.
Incubate in 1% hydrogen peroxide in methanol for 15 min.
Wash in 1 x PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100, 3 times for 5 min each.
Add 6 drops of streptavidin solution from the Streptavidin/Biotin Blocking Kit, incubate for 25 min.
Wash in 1 x PBS for 5 min.
Add 6 drops of biotin solution from the Streptavidin/Biotin Blocking Kit, incubate for 15 min.
Remove the biotin solution without washing.
Add 0.5 ml of Carbo-free reagent, incubate for 30 min.
Remove the Carbo-free reagent without washing.
Incubate with 10 μg/ml biotinylated WFA in 1× PBS for 30 min.
Prepare ABC solution at this point.
Wash in 1 x PBS/0.05% Tween-20 twice for 5 min.
Incubate for 30 min in Vectastain Elite ABC Kit: 1:100 Reagent A, 1:100 Reagent B, in 0.3% Triton X-100/1 x PBS.
Wash in 1 x PBS/0.05% Tween-20 three times for 5 min.
Incubate for 10 min with appropriate fluorescent dye diluted 1:62.5 in amplification diluent.
Wash in 1 x PBS, twice for 5 min.
Place tissue on Colorfrost Plus slides and let dry overnight.
Coverslip with a mounting medium compatible with immunofluorescence microscopy (e.g., Vectashield mounting medium, FluorSave).
